public_rationale: Reported positive compute margins matter under an inference-cost interpretation. They do not establish that price increases cover full costs while retaining customers. Conversely, losses would not prove that such prices are impossible. The undefined accounting basis and missing price, cost and demand comparison leave the causal claim unresolved.
limitations: The financial evidence is secondary reporting, not a published financial statement.
Breakeven has materially different possible meanings.
The affordability prediction is probabilistic and has no stated threshold.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The lack of utility and product differentiation means OpenAI can't raise its prices above breakeven, which would also likely make its generative AI unaffordable and unattractive to both business and personal customers.

statement.excerpt: These realities — the lack of utility and product differentiation — also mean that OpenAI can’t raise its prices above the breakeven point, which would also likely make its generative AI unaffordable and unattractive to both business and personal customers.

from_speaker: the lack of utility and product differentiation
OpenAI can’t raise its prices above the breakeven point
would also likely make its generative AI unaffordable and unattractive
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that insufficient customer value and differentiation prevent commercially viable price increases sufficient to cover the full costs of supplying OpenAI's services.
The firm claim concerns pricing power; the affordability consequence is explicitly hedged.
Full-cost breakeven is an evaluator interpretation. Covering inference costs alone and achieving company-wide profitability are different measures.
The quoted claim supplies no accounting basis for breakeven. The surrounding subscription-loss discussion does not define one.
This is assessed as an asserted causal constraint, without inventing a forecast deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Matched price, full-cost and customer-demand evidence establishes that prices sufficient for breakeven cannot retain viable demand because of inadequate utility or differentiation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched evidence shows that OpenAI raised relevant prices above full-cost breakeven while retaining viable paying demand. The accounting basis must first be resolved.

evidence.explanation: The article reports positive and improving margins after inference costs for paying users, citing The Information. This is relevant counterevidence to an inference-cost reading, but it does not establish full-cost breakeven, price increases or customer retention; no public primary financial record was retrieved.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A defined breakeven basis and matched product-level prices, costs and retention records, with evidence identifying why customers accept or reject the prices.
